source_text: «Ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πιστεύσητε, οὐδ' οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, φησί. Προσβολὴ γὰρ ἡ πίστις, εἰς σύνεσιν ἀποφέρουσα, καὶ οἱονεὶ πρὸς παραδοχὴν τοῦ θείου φωτὸς ἁπλοῦσα τὸν νοῦν. Ἐνδελεχισμοῦ δὲ ὀνομάζει τὸ θυμίαμα. Καιρὸς γὰρ οὐδεὶς, καθ' ὃν οὐκ εὐωδιάζει Χριστὸς ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ, τουτέστιν, ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ. Ἀποφάσκει δὲ παντελῶς, τὸ δεῖν ἐπ' αὐτοῦ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ Χριστοῦ, σπονδὴν κατακεῖσθαι, καὶ ἀναφέ[ρε]σθαι κάρπωμα. Κατήργηται γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ τὰ ἐν νόμῳ, καὶ εἰς τέλος ἕρπουσιν αἱ σκιαί. Τοῦτο, οἶμαι, ἔστι σπονδὴ καὶ κάρπωμα. Καὶ μαρτυρεῖ λέγων ὁ προφήτης· «Ἐξῆρται ἐξ οἴκου Κυρίου θυσία καὶ σπονδή.» Ἀναδεδειγμένης γὰρ ἤδη τῆς ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ προσκυνήσεως καὶ λατρείας, περιτταί πως αἱ σκιαὶ, καὶ τὸ ἐν τύποις εἰκαῖον καὶ ἀνόνητον παντελῶς· καινὴ γὰρ κτίσις ἐν Χριστῷ. Τῆς γὰρ χάριτος ἐκπεπτώκασιν οἱ ἐν νόμω δικαιούμενοι μετὰ τὴν τῆς ἀληθείας ἀνάδειξιν. «Οὐκ ἀνοίσεις δὲ,» φησὶν, «ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον θυμίαμα ἕτερον.» Παραδεξόμεθα γὰρ ἐν Χριστῷ ἕτερον παντελῶς οὐδένα. Ῥαββὶ δὲ τῶν ὄντων ἐροῦμεν οὐδενί. Εἷς γὰρ ἡμῶν διδάσκαλος καὶ καθηγητὴς, καὶ αὐτῷ δὴ μόνῳ προσκεισόμεθα, λέγοντες, «Μῦρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σου. Διὰ τοῦτο νεάνιδες ἠγάπησάν σε. Εἵλκυσάν με, ὀπίσω σου εἰς ὀσμὴν μύρων σου δραμοῦσαι.» Ἢ οὐχὶ τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ, «Οὐκ ἀνοίσεις ἐπ' αὐτὸ θυμίαμα ἕτερον;» Μόνου γὰρ Χριστοῦ τὸ εὐῶδες ἐν Ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῖς γε ἀληθῶς ἐχέφροσιν ἐξαρκοίη ἂν, ἑτέρας ὀσμῆς οὐκ ἐφιεμένοις· καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ οἱ τάλανες Ἰουδαῖοι. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ θυμίαμα τὸ σύνθετον καὶ λεπτὸν, τουτέστι, Χριστὸν, ταῖς ἀπονοίαις περιυβρίζουσιν. Καὶ ἀμέτοχοι μὲν τῆς ἱερᾶς ταύτης ἢ καὶ θείας ἀληθῶς μεμενήκασιν εὐωδίας· ἕτερον δὲ ἀντ' αὐτοῦ παραδέξονται, τὸν τῆς ἀνομίας υἱὸν, «τὸν ἀντικείμενον καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενον ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον Θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύοντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἐστὶ Θεὸς,» ὃς καὶ τὴν θείαν σκηνὴν καταμιαίνει, καπνὸς ὢν ἀλλότριος, καὶ ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω, κακοσμία διαβολική· «Ἔσται γὰρ αὐτοῦ,» φησὶν, «ἡ παρουσία κατ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι ὃ φής. Καὶ γάρ ἐστιν ἐναργὴς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἐξιλάσασθαί γε μὴν ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος, προστάττει τῷ Ἀαρὼν ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ καταχρίοντι τῷ αἵματι τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, τὰς τῶν κεράτων ἀρχάς. «Ἅγιον γὰρ,» φησὶ, «τῶν ἁγίων ἐστί.» Καὶ τοῦτό σοι σαφὲς καταστήσει, λέγων, ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος· «Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν μελλόντων ἀγαθῶν, διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελεωτέρας σκηνῆς, οὐ χειροποιήτου, τουτέστιν, οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως· οὐδὲ δι' αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς τὰ ἅγια, αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑ
pass_a_gloss: [Continues Cyril's turn from §18.] Isa 7:9 LXX: ean mē pisteusēte, oud' ou mē synēte = if you do not believe, you will not understand. prosbolē (first approach/onset) = faith; leads (apopherousa) to synesis (understanding); haplousa ton noun = spreads open the mind to paradochē (reception) of the divine light. endelechismou thymiama = incense of continuity/perpetual incense; no kairos when Christ does not euōdiazei (give fragrance) in the holy skēnē = the Church. apophaskei pantelōs = he utterly forbids spondēn (libation) to be laid on it and karpōma (burnt/whole offering) to be offered; 'it' = the altar, i.e. Christ. katērgētai (abolished) in Christ ta en nomō; the skiai creep eis telos. This (I think) is [what] spondē and karpōma [mean]. Prophet (Joel 1:9 LXX): exērtai (taken away) from the house of the Lord thysia and spondē. Since proskynēsis and latreia in spirit and truth have been shown, the shadows are perittai (superfluous); what is in types is eikaion (futile) and anonēton (useless); kainē ktisis in Christ. Those dikaioumenoi in law after the anadeixis of truth ekpeptōkasin (have fallen out of) grace. 'You shall not offer other incense on the altar.' We will accept no other in Christ; we will say 'Rabbi' to none of beings; one didaskalos and kathēgētēs; to him alone we will cling (proskeisometha), saying Song 1:3-4 LXX: myron ekkenōthen (ointment emptied out) your name; therefore neanides loved you; they drew me (heilkysan me), having run (dramousai) after you to the scent of your ointments. Or is this not 'you shall not offer other incense on it'? Christ's euōdes alone in the Church suffices for the truly echephrones (sensible), not desiring another osmē, as indeed the talanes (wretched) Jews [do]. The syntheton and lepton incense = Christ, they periybrizousin (outrage) tais aponoiais (in their follies). They have remained ametochoi of this sacred, or truly divine, euōdia; another they will receive in his place, the son of anomia, 2 Thess 2:4: who opposes and exalts himself over every so-called god or sebasma, so that he sits in the naos of God, showing himself that he is God; he defiles (katamiainei) the divine tent, being kapnos allotrios (alien smoke), and so to speak kakosmia diabolikē (devilish stench). 2 Thess 2:9: his parousia will be kat' energeian of Satan. PALL: I understand what you say; the logos is enargēs (clear). CYR: exilasasthai (to propitiate/make atonement) on the altar of incense he commands Aaron hapax tou eniautou (once a year), smearing (katachrionti) with the blood of katharismos of sins the archai (tips) of the horns; for it is hagion tōn hagiōn. thespesios (inspired) Paul makes it clear, Heb 9:11-12: Christ paragenomenos archiereus of the coming goods, through the greater and more perfect skēnē, not cheiropoiētos, i.e. not of this creation; not through blood of goats and calves but through his own blood eisēlthen ephapax into the holies, aiōnian lytrōsin heuramenos (having found/obtained eternal redemption).

This (I think) is [what] σπονδή and κάρπωμα [mean]. Prophet (Joel 1:9 LXX): ἐξῆρται (taken away) from the house of the Lord θυσία and σπονδή. Since προσκύνησις and λατρεία in spirit and truth have been shown, the shadows are περιτταί (superfluous); what is in types is εἰκαῖον (futile) and ἀνόνητον (useless); καινὴ κτίσις in Christ. Those δικαιούμενοι in law after the ἀνάδειξις of truth ἐκπεπτώκασιν (have fallen out of) grace. 'You shall not offer other incense on the altar.' We will accept no other in Christ; we will say 'Rabbi' to none of beings; one διδάσκαλος and καθηγητής; to him alone we will cling (προσκεισόμεθα), saying Song 1:3-4 LXX: μύρον ἐκκενωθέν (ointment emptied out) your name; therefore νεάνιδες loved you; they drew me (εἵλκυσάν με), having run (δραμοῦσαι) after you to the scent of your ointments. Or is this not 'you shall not offer other incense on it'? Christ's εὐῶδες alone in the Church suffices for the truly ἐχέφρονες (sensible), not desiring another ὀσμή, as indeed the τάλανες (wretched) Jews [do]. The σύνθετον and λεπτόν incense = Christ, they περιυβρίζουσιν (outrage) ταῖς ἀπονοίαις (in their follies). They have remained ἀμέτοχοι of this sacred, or truly divine, εὐωδία; another they will receive in his place, the son of ἀνομία, 2 Thess 2:4: who opposes and exalts himself over every so-called god or σέβασμα, so that he sits in the ναός of God, showing himself that he is God; he defiles (καταμιαίνει) the divine tent, being καπνὸς ἀλλότριος (alien smoke), and so to speak κακοσμία διαβολική (devilish stench). 2 Thess 2:9: his παρουσία will be κατ' ἐνέργειαν of Satan. PALL: I understand what you say; the λόγος is ἐναργής (clear). CYR: ἐξιλάσασθαι (to propitiate/make atonement) on the altar of incense he commands Aaron ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ (once a year), smearing (καταχρίοντι) with the blood of καθαρισμός of sins the ἀρχαί (tips) of the horns; for it is ἅγιον τῶν ἁγίων. θεσπέσιος (inspired) Paul makes it clear, Heb 9:11-12: Christ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεύς of the coming goods, through the greater and more perfect σκηνή, not χειροποίητος, i.e. not of this creation; not through blood of goats and calves but through his own blood εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ into the holies, αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος (having found/obtained eternal redemption).
pass_b_english: Cyril: ‘For if you do not believe, neither will you understand,’ (Isaiah 7:9) he says. For faith is the first approach that leads on to understanding, and it opens the mind, as it were, to receive the divine light. He calls the incense ‘perpetual’ (Exodus 30:8), for there is no time when Christ does not give off his fragrance in the holy tent, that is, in the Church. And he altogether forbids any drink offering to be poured out on it, or any burnt offering to be offered up on it (Exodus 30:9), meaning, clearly, on the altar, which is Christ. For in Christ the things of the law have been abolished, and the shadows are drawing to their end. That, I think, is what the drink offering and the burnt offering stand for. The prophet bears witness when he says, ‘Sacrifice and drink offering have been taken away from the house of the Lord’ (Joel 1:9). For now that worship and service in spirit and truth (John 4:23–24) have been revealed, the shadows are in a sense superfluous, and whatever is done in types is futile and wholly useless; for in Christ there is a new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17). For those who would be justified in the law after the truth has been revealed have fallen away from grace (Galatians 5:4). ‘You shall not offer,’ he says, ‘other incense on the altar’ (Exodus 30:9). For in Christ we will accept no other whatever. We will call no one at all ‘Rabbi,’ for we have one Teacher and Master (Matthew 23:8–10), and to him alone we will hold fast, saying, ‘Your name is perfume poured out; therefore the maidens have loved you. They drew me; they ran after you toward the fragrance of your perfumes’ (Song of Songs 1:3–4). Or is this not what is meant by ‘You shall not offer other incense on it’ (Exodus 30:9)? For to those who are truly sensible, the fragrance of Christ alone in the Church would be enough; they long for no other scent, whereas the wretched Jews certainly do. For in their folly they heap insults on the compounded and finely ground incense, that is, on Christ. They have remained without any share in this sacred, or rather truly divine, fragrance; but they will receive another in his place, the son of lawlessness, ‘who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God,’ as it is written, ‘proclaiming himself to be God’ (2 Thessalonians 2:3–4). He also defiles the divine tent, since he is foreign smoke and, if I may put it so, a devilish stench. ‘For his coming,’ it says, ‘will be by the working of Satan’ (2 Thessalonians 2:9).
Palladius: I understand what you mean, for the argument is plain.

Cyril: Further, he commands Aaron to make atonement on the altar of incense once a year, smearing the tips of its horns with the blood of the purification of sins. ‘For it is,’ he says, ‘holy of holies’ (Exodus 30:10). The inspired Paul will make this clear to you when he says: ‘But when Christ came as High Priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made with hands, that is, not of this creation, not through the blood of goats and bulls but through his own blood, he entered once for all into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption’ (Hebrews 9:11–12).

choices.why: μόσχων in Hebrews 9:12 is rendered 'bulls' to match the μόσχος of Leviticus 4 that §20 reads against it.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

The first paragraph continues Cyril's turn from §18 (which ends on a full sentence); it carries the 'Cyril:' label like the other Book 9 rows. Isaiah 7:9 is the LXX reading ('you will not understand'); the Hebrew has 'you will not stand firm'. The section ends mid-word in the Greek (εὑ|ράμενος, Hebrews 9:12); the whole participle 'having obtained eternal redemption' is rendered here, so §20 opens with Romans 6. Exodus 30:9 LXX reads 'You shall not offer other incense on it, a burnt offering, a sacrifice; and you shall not pour a drink offering on it'; Cyril paraphrases the libation and burnt-offering clause before quoting the incense clause twice. 'Son of lawlessness' blends 2 Thessalonians 2:3 ('man of lawlessness ... son of perdition'); the cite covers 2:3-4. 'They will receive another in his place' may echo John 5:43; left uncited as doubtful. 'Abolished in Christ' may echo 2 Corinthians 3:14; left uncited. Cyril's Song of Songs text has 'they drew me ... having run' where Rahlfs LXX has 'they drew you ... we will run'; rendered as Cyril has it. LXX and English verse numbers agree for Song of Songs 1:3-4. 'Wretched' renders τάλανες in Cyril's anti-Jewish polemic; kept as written, not softened or sharpened. 'Holy of holies' (Exodus 30:10, 'most holy') is kept literal because §20 builds on it ('Christ ... the Holy of Holies by nature'). μόσχων in Hebrews 9:12 is rendered 'bulls' to match the μόσχος of Leviticus 4 that §20 reads against it.

changes: added 'Cyril:' label to the continuation paragraph (matches the other Book 9 rows)
'offered there' -> 'offered up on it' (ἀναφέρεσθαι ... ἐπ' αὐτοῦ)
'shadows are creeping toward their end' -> 'drawing to their end' (stiff calque of ἕρπουσιν)
restored γάρ: 'For those who would be justified' (Galatians 5:4)
'no one in the world' -> 'no one at all' (τῶν ὄντων οὐδενί; 'world' was added)
'as the wretched Jews certainly do' -> 'whereas the wretched Jews certainly do' (old wording could be read as the Jews also not longing for another scent)
Hebrews 9:12 μόσχων 'calves' -> 'bulls' for consistency with §20, as the translator note already claimed
